bridge: Introduce 'stop blocks' as primitives: tape/clip a stop at a tick to turn the ruler into a repeatability jig.
Introduce an insert medium (sand, rice, gel) to create a quasi-granular/tunable fingertip 'sensor pad'.
Introduce a 'flip-to-compare' comparator: mount A and B in adjacent ring-registered pages and alternate quickly to amplify differences.
Introduce the 'geometry gauge' primitive: cut notches/holes at known sizes to create a quick fit/spacing reference tool.
Introduce a 'probe+record' primitive: use the tip to find a location, then lock that geometry by bending a stop so it becomes a reusable gauge.
Introduce a 'preload cradle' primitive: cut geometry creates a self-centering cradle that holds parts by gentle compression.
